briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: New Doors Open in Ann Arbor While D.C. Fast-Tracks Psilocybin and Congress Buys Hemp More Time
briefs.top: Michigan operators got real reasons for optimism this week — Lume and New Standard both opened new Ann Arbor doors even as the 24% wholesale tax fight heads for a September court date, and the GOP's gubernatorial nominee is now campaigning on a tax rollback. Nationally, Compass Pathways' psilocybin therapy is racing toward an early 2027 launch on an FDA fast-track, and Congress just bought the hemp industry another month to negotiate a real regulatory framework instead of a ban.

local.text: Lume Cannabis Co. opened its new Ann Arbor location at 2247 W. Liberty Street with a three-day grand opening, adding another Tree Town storefront even as the market absorbs tax pressure.

New Standard opened a new Ann Arbor dispensary this month, running giveaways and discounts for its Sept. 3-6 opening weekend — fresh proof operators are still investing in Michigan's flagship college-town market.

Michigan's GOP gubernatorial nominee John James is campaigning on cutting the cannabis excise tax and rolling back the 24% wholesale levy, giving operators a real electoral path to relief in November alongside Democratic primary rival Chris Swanson's earlier repeal pledge.

Rize, a three-store U.P. operator, is countering the wholesale tax by negotiating cost-sharing splits with suppliers rather than absorbing the hit alone — a playbook other multi-location brands can copy while the second wholesale-tax lawsuit heads toward a September trial.

Michigan's 24% wholesale tax generated $37.38 million in the second quarter — up from Q1's $34 million — while Fields Cannary, a Muskegon dispensary-and-restaurant hospitality buildout, is targeting a fall opening that pushes the format further than most Michigan stores have gone.

national.text: Compass Pathways confirmed its rolling NDA for COMP360 psilocybin is on track for a Q4 2026 filing after the FDA granted it a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher, shrinking review time to 1-2 months and putting a commercial launch within reach for the first half of 2027.

The FDA's April National Priority Vouchers also went to Usona Institute (psilocybin for major depressive disorder) and Transcend Therapeutics (methylone for PTSD), signaling the agency is fast-tracking a whole class of psychedelic medicines, not just one company's drug.

Congress passed a stopgap funding bill 370-48 that pushes the federal hemp-THC recriminalization deadline from November 12 to December 11, giving brands and retailers more runway to lobby for a regulated three-tier framework instead of an outright ban.

DEA's marijuana rescheduling hearing wrapped its closing-argument stage in late August, with the administrative record now built out enough that operators should start prepping the compliance paperwork DEA is already requesting from early-mover states like Colorado.
national.source: The Cannabis Business Advisors / Marijuana Moment

national.text: FDA finalized its guidance for psychedelic drug clinical trials and scheduled a September 14 public hearing on the future therapeutic use of psychedelics — regulatory scaffolding that one treating physician says could let psilocybin therapy "wipe out the SSRIs" if durability holds.
